kind_of_thing.quote: The mustard plant is any one of several plant species in the genera Brassica, Rhamphospermum and Sinapis in the family Brassicaceae (the mustard family).

extinct.quote: Mild white mustard (Sinapis hirta) grows wild in North Africa, the Middle East and Mediterranean Europe and has spread farther by long cultivation; brown or Indian mustard (B. juncea), originally from the foothills of the Himalaya, is grown commercially in the UK, Canada and the US; black mustard (B. nigra) in Argentina, Chile, the US and some European countries.

kind_of_plant.quote: Many vegetables are cultivated varieties of mustard plants; domestication may have begun 6,000 years ago.

part_we_eat.quote: Some kinds of mustard plants have edible leaves.
